title: performance-canary: automated regression detection + hysteresis rollout guards
author: Priya Shah
description: Motivation: Our continuous perf canary detected multiple noisy alerts and manual rollbacks over the past quarter. This PR adds automated regression detection with configurable hysteresis and rollout guards to reduce noisy rollouts and prevent transient spikes from triggering global rollbacks. What changed: 1) perf/canary/detector.py - new detector that computes p50/p95 deltas against a moving baseline, supports latency and throughput metrics, and exposes reason codes for rollback. 2) perf/canary/hysteresis.py - hysteresis state machine that requires N consecutive detections across T window before gating a rollout. 3) perf/canary/config.yaml - new knobs: latency_regression_pct, throughput_drop_pct, consecutive_detections, window_seconds, critical_tier_threshold. 4) observability/dashboards/perf_canary.json - dashboard with canary health, alert history, and rollback reasons. 5) deploy/k8s/canary-controller.yaml - controller changes to perform automatic traffic shifts and rollback when guards trip. 6) tests/perf/test_canary_detector.py + integration load tests - added coverage and synthetic regression scenarios. Rollout behavior: canary traffic is shifted in stages (1%, 5%, 20%) with evaluation at each stage; detector must not observe > latency_regression_pct (default 5%) or sustained throughput drop > 8% for the hysteresis window (default 10 minutes with 3 consecutive detections) to proceed. If the critical_tier_threshold is exceeded (e.g., user-visible p95 > 15% regression on production traffic), auto-rollback is triggered immediately and an incident stub is created. Backwards compatibility: defaults preserve current rollout timings; this change is configurable per-service. Testing: unit tests, synthetic load integration tests in CI, and staged rollout to staging and canary in prod for 48h. Monitoring: added new metrics (canary.detections, canary.hysteresis_state, canary.rollback_reasons) and dashboards + alert rules. Migration: ops can tune config via the Console or edit the perf/canary/config.yaml in infra repo. Security: no user data is surfaced outside telemetry. See linked Linear tickets for rollout plan and post-deploy verification.
commits: detector: implement baseline delta detection and reason codes
hysteresis: add state machine and persistence for consecutive detections
config: add canary detection knobs and defaults
observability: dashboard + metrics for canary detection
k8s: canary controller integration and rollout guard hooks
tests: add unit + integration synthetic regression tests
review_comments: Ethan Cole: Please ensure the detector uses percentile bucketing consistent with our existing telemetry to avoid skew when sampling across regions. Response (Priya): detector reuses telemetry percentile buckets and includes per-region baselines.

Marta Ruiz: Hysteresis state must be persisted across controller restarts; otherwise we risk flapping. Response (Priya): hysteresis state stored in controller-backed KV (etcd) with TTL; added tests to simulate restarts.

Liu Chen: Can we provide a safety margin for small services with low QPS to avoid false positives? Response (Priya): added min_sample_count and a QPS floor in config; services under threshold bypass auto-rollback and only surface alerts.
Marta Ruiz: Approved after CI green and testing in staging. Ethan Cole: Approved. Liu Chen: Approved.
release_notes: Add automatic performance regression detection for canary rollouts with configurable thresholds
Introduce hysteresis to reduce noisy rollbacks (consecutive detection window)
New rollout guards that can trigger immediate rollback on critical regressions
New metrics and dashboard for canary health and rollback reasons
Configurable per-service knobs: latency_regression_pct, throughput_drop_pct, consecutive_detections, window_seconds
summary_metrics: min_sample_count: 200 (default floor to avoid low-QPS false positives)
testing: unit tests for detector and hysteresis logic
integration synthetic load tests simulating latency and throughput regressions
staging canary smoke run for 48h with real traffic shadowing
manual verification steps documented in docs/perf/canary.md
